title: Distribution attribution rests on a per-Instance Reward Code paired with a Tracking Methodology
content:
Every Distribution Reward Instance carries exactly two substantive parameters: a Reward Code and a Tracking Methodology. The codes are per-venue — Sky.money App `1` (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.1.1.1), Open Source Widgets `0`, DeFi Saver `1002`, CoW Swap `1003`, ParaSwap `1004`, Yearn (Gimme) `1007`, MOM `1015`, Lazy Summer Protocol `1016`.

The pair is the whole attribution mechanism. The Reward Code is the identifier a venue stamps on the demand it originates; the Tracking Methodology is the rule that says which on-chain events are counted and how. Neither works alone: a code with no methodology has no observation rule, and a methodology with no code cannot separate one venue's flow from another's.

Putting both in the Instance's Parameters — rather than in an off-chain agreement — means the measurement basis of a commercial relationship is part of the governed Artifact. A partner disputing its payment can point to the exact provision that defines what counts, and changing the basis is an Artifact edit rather than a business decision.

The numbering carries a hint of structure: first-party surfaces occupy the low integers (`1` and `0`) while third-party partners sit in a `100x`/`101x` band assigned in onboarding order. It also means the code space itself is ecosystem-wide state — codes must not collide across Agents for attribution to work.
description: Each venue gets its own code (Sky.money App `1`, DeFi Saver `1002`, CoW Swap `1003`, MOM `1015`) plus a named methodology defining which on-chain events count as that venue's demand.
